physics_notes:
# green_straw_tumbler

Built from the supplied offline kitchen capture. Dimensions are **0.089 × 0.089 × 0.196 m**, in XYZ order, with 1 mapped inventory instances. Blender and OBJ use metres and +Z up; GLB converts to +Y up. The origin is the bottom support centre of the upright vessel, even for inverted/horizontal instances.

## Evidence and registration

Source crops and calibrated camera matrices are retained in `evidence/` and `spec.json`. Per-instance `measurement` stores the clicked pixel and unmodified depth-derived surface point. Vessel-centre offsets, support heights, stack offsets, and transparent-object corrections are explicit in `model.json`. These are measured-plus-inferred rest placements, not exact tracked trajectories. Yaw for rotationally symmetric items is arbitrary; handle/print azimuth remains approximate.

The global metric scale comes from supplied WORLD calibration (0.1632594913 m per reconstruction unit); no tape measurement was supplied. Reported depth accuracy is about 4%, but the actual opposite-edge checks disagree by more than that on glass/metal and across views. Allow roughly 10–25% dimensional uncertainty and 4–6 cm placement uncertainty, increasing to 8–12 cm for the microwave-top matcha/tankard and hanging-glass registration failures. Those overlays do not establish an accurate world fit. `../evidence/edge_measurements.json` retains the raw checks, and `../evidence/support_measurements.json` retains support fits. Final sizes balance those measurements with visible proportions and the supplied inventory priors.

Three freely movable rigid bodies: hollow cup, removable lid, and straw. The straw is visually hollow but uses a solid slender convex collider. Printed branding is too blurred for exact reproduction.

## Contact and physics

Collision uses one base and convex wall sectors (or four box walls), preserving a central opening. Convex hulls approximate curved profiles and reduce clearance near the wall; they are not a liquid boundary. Mug handles use three convex pieces preserving an opening. Each collider is stored separately and assigned to its rigid body in `model.json`; Blender uses compound rigid bodies. Loose lids/straws remain independent with no false one-axis joint. No breaking, deformability, fluid, seal compliance, clip snap forces, thermal effects or friction calibration is modeled.

Dry mass 0.19 kg and friction 0.4 are guesses. Glaze, glass IOR, transmission and roughness are priors. Photo crops supply appearance microvariation and selected decals; those are not measured reflectance maps. `validation.json` records convexity, watertightness and triangle checks. The 2,176-triangle visual mesh is below 80k.

## Review and reproduction

`review.jpg` pairs real crops with renders from the supplied cameras, plus beauty and interior views. Only the first instance is rendered in each calibrated comparison; source stacks, hands, contents and lighting are not synthesized. A blank/misaligned calibrated crop is a registration limitation, not a successful fit. No silhouette accuracy or task-success score is claimed.

Run Blender 4.2 with `blender -b -P build.py` in this folder. Build script, spec and textures are self-contained. Set-level preparation and reporting scripts retain measurement provenance. Measured build/render wall time is recorded in `model.json`; reconstruction throughput and online latency were not measured. This is offline analysis of an existing capture.

## Realism QA repair (2026-10-12)

Three-view evidence: f1367, f1371, f1342. Mean visible silhouette IoU: 0.8401. Scope: all stored instances.

- Removed visual/collider name collisions so lid, straw and clip lookups resolve to physical visual parts
- Subdivided long shell faces to eliminate false lensing from interpolated normals; preserved physical transmission/IOR
- Rebuilt standalone build.py, GLB, Blender, visual parts and segmented convex collision
- Added structured physics with explicit assumptions, fragility, centre of mass and friction
- Added three fixed calibrated camera comparisons, masks, silhouette IoU and RGB histograms
- Extended straw above removable lid; added visible photographed branding; retained separate cup/lid/straw bodies

Remaining (strict A/B acceptance is not met):

- Seal fit and straw-hole clearance unmeasured; hidden taper inferred
- Product identity/dry weight not verified; mass, friction and restitution are engineering priors
- Lighting/environment and transparent-object backgrounds only approximated; histogram mismatch is not a recovered albedo error
- No robot grasp, drop/breakage or complete scene stack/rack dynamics validation
- Silhouette target A/B not met in fixed calibrated cameras; per-view camera/image residual remains visible

`model.json.physics` is authoritative for current priors. Older prose above describes the pre-QA reconstruction. `../review/green_straw_tumbler_compare.jpg` is the current calibrated comparison.

physics_properties.mass_basis: Closed visual-shell volume times documented material density; excludes open decals; not a manufacturer weight
physics_properties.centre_of_mass_basis: Volume-weighted closed connected shells only; open label/decal planes excluded. Uniform density per shell remains approximate.

provenance.geometry: Reconstructed from kitchen video; hidden surfaces are completed. Scale and material appearance remain approximate.
provenance.motion: Observed trajectories where documented; unobserved axes and endpoints are assumptions.
provenance.forces: Simulation measurements of assumed parameters; not force measurements from video.

visual_bindings_note: Visuals use the latest asset revision; mechanism geometry may predate it. Body rest offsets preserve the visual placement.
